name: pulumi-landscape-platform-py-migration
instr:
Landscape's production platform is already imported into the Pulumi stack `dev`, but `/workspace/pulumi` only has a placeholder program, so a preview today plans to delete everything. It needs a faithful Python port of the Terraform in `/workspace/terraform`, with `__main__.py` as the entry point.

Against the imported stack, a preview must show no changes, with Terraform's root outputs exported under the same names and values. Keep exactly the URNs the stack has: one component per module call (`landscape:modules:Network` named `network`, likewise `platform`, `data` and `workloads`) as the parent of that module's resources, each named after its Terraform resource plus `-<key>` for `for_each` instances. Each root variable in `variables.tf` becomes a config key of the same name, such as `landscape-platform:availability_zones`, with the same value in YAML and Terraform's default when unset. For any variable values Terraform and AWS accept, a preview must plan the same creates, updates, replacements and deletes, with the same settings and outputs, as `terraform plan` with those values. That includes Terraform's defaults for unset arguments, even where Pulumi's differ; lexicographic key order wherever Terraform turns a map into a list; later maps winning in `merge()`; and every cross-resource reference wired through outputs, so values are unknown in a preview exactly where Terraform says known after apply, element by element in lists. Settings changed outside Pulumi must be planne
